title: Integral tensor model of one finite condensed complex
statement: Let ell be prime and X a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with ell invertible in every stalk. Use the native section-ring and section-module functor S of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data], with its specified commutative, additive and finite-exact structures. Let E be a finite intermediate field of PadicAlgCl ell and C any normalized coefficient presentation of its canonical size transport E_small. For every bounded constructible condensed E-module complex K [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], there exists an integral constructible complex L over E_small such that derived extension of L along C.integralMap is isomorphic to S applied to inverse native encoding of the derived extension of K from E to PadicAlgCl ell. The native encoding is the specified coefficient-isomorphism encoding, not a newly chosen equivalence.

proof.text: Transport E along its canonical size equivalence. The continuous-function coefficient identification and the internal/section-module equivalence transport the condensed finite-stage object to rational coefficient modules. Local finite presentation on each stratum becomes finite local freeness by the finite-field local-triviality theorem, including rank zero. Exactness transports bounded cohomology.

proof.text: Apply the essential-image clause of continuous_rational_derived_realization at this same finite field. Its raw rationalization has the original integral objects. Transport the resulting integral representative to the framework integral category using integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed and its quotient-normalized coefficient comparison.

proof.text: The integral tensor identity of finite realization, followed by scalar extension to PadicAlgCl, identifies the realized object. Pointwise and residue normalization identify its structural map with C.integralMap. Balanced tensor associativity gives the required isomorphism. The specified native encoding and exact section-module equivalence identify the right side with inverse encoding followed by S. No global algebraic-closure object descent is used in this lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem condensedFinite_integralTensor_model
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [Fact (∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim X ≤ n)]
    [Fact (∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x))]
    [IsCommMonObj (abRing l X)] [(sections l X).Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (sections l X)] [PreservesFiniteColimits (sections l X)]
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    (C : CoefficientPresentation l X (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) (embedding l E))
    (K : ProEtale.PadicSubfieldConstructible X l E) :
    ∃ L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) X,
      Nonempty ((pbcDerivedExtend (C.integralMap l X)).obj L.obj ≅
        (sections l X).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          ((ProEtale.NativeEncoding.derivedEncoding l X).inv.obj
            ((ProEtale.derivedExtendScalarsToPadicAlgCl X l E).obj K.obj)))
